method: Validation for the new cfgver-scaling-diagnostics skill (v18 eval set addition: Q103-Q108). Per skill-routing-maintenance's cost-scoping guidance, ran the new skill's should-trigger queries plus its two nearest-neighbor adversarial checks (rocq-timeout-triage, cfgver-executor) and two regression guards against the two body-only cross-reference additions (cfgver hub's module-map table, rocq-timeout-triage's Step 4 handoff bullet) -- not a full sweep. One routing-judge agent (haiku) per query, 47-entry listing (25 full-description + 10 name-only tier-2 via skillOverrides + 12 rocq: plugin commands) inlined in every prompt.
note: Q105's first pass returned the correct verdict (rocq-timeout-triage) but TOTAL=46 against a 47-entry listing -- a bad checksum per the agent's own rule (a verdict whose TOTAL is wrong is discarded regardless of whether the answer looks right). Re-ran with a fresh independent judge; second pass returned TOTAL=47/rocq-timeout-triage, matching. All other five queries returned TOTAL=47 on the first pass.

summary: 6/6 pass, no regressions. cfgver-scaling-diagnostics fires on its should-trigger territory (Q103/Q104) and correctly loses both adversarial near-misses (Q105 to rocq-timeout-triage, Q106 to cfgver-executor) and both regression guards (Q107, Q108) -- the two body-only cross-reference edits (cfgver hub, rocq-timeout-triage handoff) caused no routing changes elsewhere. Description needs no tuning. Skill is tier-1 by default (absent from settings.json's skillOverrides), which is the correct placement given it must compete directly with rocq-timeout-triage/cfgver-executor on its own description rather than being reached only by name from a parent.
